title: per-service-dampener-and-transient-suppressor-to-reduce-pager-churn
author: Morgan Chen
release_notes: Add per-service dampening and transient suppression to incident-bot to reduce noisy alerts; configurable defaults and canary rollout; no breaking changes by default.
body:
Motivation: On-call teams have reported high pager churn caused by short-lived metric spikes and flapping alerts from third-party services. This PR introduces a per-service dampener and a transient-suppressor policy in incident-bot to reduce noisy pages while preserving actionable incidents.

Summary of changes: adds a new ServiceDampener policy engine which tracks recent alert emissions per service and suppresses repeat pages inside a configurable quiet window; implements a TransientSuppressor stage that defers notifications for rules with low-confidence signals for a short evaluation window; exposes service-level configuration via the incident-bot config store and Console feature flag for canary rollout; includes unit and e2e tests and a migration to populate default dampening profiles for existing services.

Key design points: default behavior is conservative — no incidents are auto-closed; only notification emissions are suppressed. Dampener is keyed by (service_id, alert_signature) and supports exponential backoff for repeated noise. TransientSuppressor stores a short-lived hypothesis for an alert (TTL ~30s by default) and will only escalate if the condition persists or additional corroborating signals arrive. Operators can override per-service thresholds and exempt critical services.

Configuration knobs added: service_config[dampener.enabled:boolean], service_config[dampener.quiet_window_seconds:int], service_config[dampener.max_backoff_seconds:int], service_config[transient.enable:boolean], service_config[transient.eval_window_seconds:int], global.feature_flags[service_dampener_canary].

Testing and rollout: unit tests included for backoff maths, suppression TTL and signature collisions. e2e test harness simulates a noisy external service to verify reduced pager counts. Rollout plan: enable canary flag for 5% of services for 48 hours, review PagerDuty incident rate delta and customer-facing SLOs, then ramp to 100% if no regression.

Security and compliance: no secrets change, audit log events added for suppressed notifications to ensure traceability.

- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Migration script for default profiles
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented
